title: Heat pump or furnace plus air conditioning? One study's medians were $270 apart.

scenes.purpose: Land the one figure the format promises: the gap between the two medians, before any framing.

visual.description: Cold open on the dark ground. One ledger tile centred in the content band, the accent rule down its left edge. The figure counts up to $270 as the question is asked and holds through the rest of the sentence; the label beneath says which way the gap runs. Nothing else on screen: no second tile, no absolute prices.

chart.title: Median installed cost, one study
chart.note: The gap between the medians, not a price: do not let it read as what either system costs, and do not imply it is a quote for one house.

scenes.direction: Hard cut in; the tile lands as the question ends and the figure counts up on "$270". Hold half a second after the last word.
scenes.narration: Heat pump, or furnace plus air conditioning? One study's median installed costs came out $270 apart.

scenes.purpose: Put the caveat on the figure in the viewer's hands: it is one study's national medians, not a quote for their house.

visual.description: The tile clears. Three short sans lines build down the content band, each with a small accent square, each landing on its own beat of the sentence: the source, then the caveat, then the result. The earlier lines dim slightly as the next arrives, so the eye stays on the newest line. No figures anywhere in the frame.

scenes.direction: Lines on "medians", "not quotes" and "landed just under". Hold the third line through the end of the sentence.
scenes.narration: Those are one study's national medians, not quotes for your house: the heat pump's median landed just under the gas furnace with air conditioning.

scenes.purpose: Show the spread the gap sits inside: the price ranges overlap, so the two medians being close is not a clean win.

visual.description: One horizontal bar, label above it, the figure at its end. The track draws in the accent from the left as the sentence names the overlap and stops with room to spare on the right, so the bar reads as a large share and not as all of it. The frame stays otherwise empty; this scene is the qualification, and it should feel like one.

chart.title: Other systems' price ranges that overlap the heat pump's
chart.note: The study says more than 80 percent, so the bar is drawn at the stated floor; it is overlap between distributions, never a share of houses or of installers.

scenes.direction: Bar fills on "overlap"; hold most of a second after the last word, so the spread sits before the disagreement arrives.
scenes.narration: More than 80 percent of the other systems' cost distributions overlap the heat pump's.

scenes.purpose: Give the other side in its own words: a model that puts heat pumps higher upfront and ahead only over the system's life.

visual.description: A paper exhibit rises into the content band, the document name and line numbers in small mono above it, the passage set in the serif. The words "Despite heat pumps having higher upfront costs" underline in the accent as they are spoken, and the clause about efficiency and doubling as cooling stays legible after them, so the reversal over the system's life is visible, not just heard.

excerpt.highlight: Despite heat pumps having higher upfront costs

scenes.direction: Page lifts in on "A Canadian model disagrees"; the highlight sweeps on "higher upfront"; hold half a second on "over the system's life".
scenes.narration: A Canadian model disagrees, putting heat pumps higher upfront than gas heating with air conditioning, ahead only over the system's life.

scenes.purpose: Name the baseline the gap depends on, so a viewer comparing against a furnace alone does not take the figure home.

visual.description: The page clears. Three sans lines build down the band on the sentence's turns: the baseline, then the subtraction, then what it does to the answer. The third line is the one to hold, and the accent square beside it is the loss colour rather than the accent, so the reversal reads at a glance on a phone.

scenes.direction: Lines on "both sides", "take the air conditioner out" and "the bigger number"; hold the third line for most of a second before the close.
scenes.narration: Cooling is counted on both sides here: take the air conditioner out of your quote, and the heat pump is the bigger number.

scenes.purpose: Close on the full inquiry; the video draws this as the end card.

visual.description: The end card the video draws itself: the seal, the full inquiry's question and the call to action. No lines of its own, no figures, nothing added over it.

scenes.direction: Cut to the end card as the sentence starts; hold it to the last word and a beat after.
scenes.narration: Which comparison fits your house is the question the full inquiry takes on.
